summary.headline: GFL Q4 FY26 chemicals revenue rose 11% YoY to INR1,358 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR353 crore; battery materials ramp and INR3,150 crore FY27 capex announced.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 chemicals revenue of INR1,358 crore (+11% YoY), EBITDA of INR353 crore (+13% YoY) and PAT of INR169 crore (+5% YoY), led by Fluoropolymers and the start of R-32 production in March 2026. Battery materials (GFCL EV) is in its startup phase, with a sharp rise in losses in the quarter because pre-operative and trial costs now run through P&L after LiPF6 capitalisation on 5 January 2026, plus a one-time forex loss on buyer's credit. Management guided to FY27 capex of INR3,150 crore (INR2,300 crore EV, INR850 crore GFL) and said battery revenue will exit FY27 Q4 in the high three-digit crore range. The call was constructive on demand but gave little quantitative detail on contract terms, qualification timelines or fluoropolymer capacity utilisation.

financial_highlights.metric: Cumulative EV capex invested to date

financial_highlights.value: Decline of about 0.5 percentage point, described as flat

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR848 crore, up 19% YoY and 14% QoQ, driven by value-added grades and higher volumes. Management expects FY27 growth of 15-20% and said newer grades (PFA, FKM) carry higher margins.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (refrigerants, bulk chemicals)
segments.commentary: R-32 production and sales began in March 2026; over 10,000 tonnes capacity is operating, with a target of 20,000 tonnes. Caustic soda and fluoromethane pricing expected to stay range-bound in FY27.

segments.name: Battery materials (GFCL EV)
segments.commentary: LiPF6 salt capitalised 5 January 2026 and now commercially selling, with full qualification at most major electrolyte players. LFP cathode final qualification expected by Q3 FY27; binders qualified at major customers. Management says all commissioned capacity is contracted and expects a 3-digit crore quarterly revenue exit rate by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total capex of INR3,150 crore: INR850 crore for GFL (INR150 crore refrigerants, INR222 crore electronic specialty chemicals, INR250 crore new fluoropolymers, INR230 crore backward integration and maintenance) and INR2,300 crore for GFCL EV.
Battery materials cumulative capex of INR6,000 crore by FY28 retained, targeting asset turns near 2x and EBITDA margins above 25%; full earnings potential expected by FY29.
Battery revenue expected to grow quarter-on-quarter with a significant rise; management expects a 3-digit crore quarterly run-rate by Q4 FY27.
Fluoropolymer volume and EBITDA growth expected to continue, with fluoropolymer demand growth of 15-20% in FY27.
Caustic soda and fluoromethane pricing expected range-bound in FY27.
Oman capex to proceed with no change in plan, per management.
capex_capacity: FY27 GFL capex INR850 crore: INR150 crore refrigerant gas capacity, INR222 crore high-purity electronic specialty chemicals for semiconductors, INR250 crore new fluoropolymer capacity, INR230 crore backward integration and maintenance.
R-32: over 10,000 tonnes achieved; target 20,000 tonnes, with ramp-up over time. No plan stated yet beyond 20,000 tonnes, though management said quota is available.

Battery materials: phase one capacity commissioned and contracted; LFP plant commissioned in early stage; natural graphite anode active material facility planned, which management said would take coverage to about 70% of LFP cell value.
Fluoropolymer capacities set up a few years ago are near optimum utilisation; new fluoropolymer capacity to be added.
Cumulative EV capex invested so far about INR1,900-2,000 crore; INR2,300 crore planned for FY27, with a similar amount likely in the following year to reach INR6,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer prices rose; management said GFL also took a price increase and kept EBITDA margins despite higher raw material and logistics costs.
Fluoropolymer demand is driven by semiconductors, EVs, BESS, hydrogen, fuel cells, electrolysers and solar; management expects FY27 growth of 15-20%.
Refrigerant demand supported by residential AC, commercial refrigeration, cold chain and AI data-centre cooling; R-32 sold domestically and in exports, with some contracts in place.
Battery: anchor customers secured across products; management would not disclose whether contracts are take-or-pay.
Inventory: working capital cycle elevated because of Germany/US warehouse stock held as insurance for JIT customers and longer voyage times (7-8 weeks versus 3-4 weeks earlier).

qa_highlights.question: Will the fluoropolymer expansion be PTFE or new grades, and how is growth split?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is in new fluoropolymers; management gave no PTFE/new split, saying earlier capacities are almost at optimum utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the battery EBITDA loss so large in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said post-operational start, pre-operative and trial costs (about INR20 crore earlier, now about INR45 crore) flow through P&L, plus a one-time forex loss on buyer's credit now fully hedged.

qa_highlights.question: How much battery revenue can the invested capex generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 2x asset turn after gestation of 9-12 months per plant; FY27 to see material salt volumes, LFP later after Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the R-32 expansion finished, and are there plans beyond 20,000 tonnes?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 10,000 tonnes operating from April; the 20,000 tonne target is still in progress. Further additions will depend on market and product mix, with quota numbers said to be clear internally.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EV capacity take-or-pay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose contract terms, saying anchor customers, agreed specs and pricing are in writing.

qa_highlights.question: Will battery revenue reach a high three-digit crore quarterly run-rate by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue will grow significantly QoQ and expects to reach a 3-digit crore figure by Q4 FY27.

risks_watch: Battery startup losses: costs now expensed with the plants capitalised; management expects them to ease but gave no timeline.
LFP cathode final qualification slated for Q3 FY27; revenue from LFP depends on it.
Working capital: inventory days rising; management attributes this to the high-stock model and longer transit times, with no target stated.
Middle East conflict: disruptions to logistics, input costs and currency, with forex swings noted as a cause of the battery loss.
R-32 ramp to 20,000 tonnes and whether it sells at expected volumes given weak Middle East demand in March.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the battery ramp, with a clear capex plan; cautious and sometimes evasive on contract terms, capacity utilisation numbers, the EBITDA of new grades and the reason for battery losses.
key_quotes: And now is the time for us to add capexes in new Fluoropolymers segment right now.
So, FY '27 will be a material quantity for salt, which I have already indicated very clearly.
It's a short-term thing because it's kind of a startup business.

growth.why: Management guides fluoropolymer volume growth of 15-20% in FY27 and battery revenue to a 3-digit crore quarterly exit rate by Q4 FY27, backed by R-32 ramp to 20,000 t, INR250 crore new fluoropolymer capacity and contracted commissioned battery capacity, though contract terms, qualification timelines and fluoropolymer utilisation detail were thin.
